How to do itPendlay Row

Start position

Right
BACK FLAT
Wrong
BACK ROUNDED

Right: Torso level, back flat, hips a little above deadlift height.

Wrong: Back rounded to reach the bar.

Top position

Right
TORSO LEVEL
Wrong
TORSO RISES

Right: Bar at chest base. Torso level, shoulders not shrugged.

Wrong: Torso risen up to yank the bar.

Keep your torso level with the floor, shoulders and hips at one height.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Back roundedThe back is rounded to reach the bar on the floor.
  2. Hips tuck underThe hips tuck under and the back curls down.
Pull1 s
Lower2 s
Look closer

Grip

Overhand, thumbs around the bar. Straps are fine if grip fails first.

Keep the wrists from curling forward.

Common handling mistakes

  • Starting with a rounded back

    Fix: Raise the bar on blocks or plates. Keep the back flat.

  • Standing partly up to yank

    Fix: Use less weight. Keep the torso level, hips not forward.

  • Elbows flared wide

    Fix: Lighten the load. Pull the bar toward the hips.

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in your upper back and sides. Hamstrings and lower back hold the position.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • FixStop the set. Don't train through the pain.

Set it up

  1. 1

    New to lifting? Start with seated or chest-supported rows first.

  2. 2

    Bar on the floor. Stand over it, feet flat, shoulder width.

  3. 3

    Hips a little above deadlift height. Overhand, slightly wider than shoulders. Brace.

  4. 4

    Back rounds to reach it? Raise the bar on blocks or plates.

  5. 5

    Beat target by one or two reps? Add 2 to 10 percent.

Risks and when to stop

  • Starting a rep with a rounded back is dangerous.
  • Of the rows tested, the bent-over row loaded the lower spine most.
  • Heavy reps with a held breath send blood pressure very high.

Back pain

How to do itLandmine Row

Back line

Right
BACK STRAIGHT
Wrong
LOWER BACK ROUNDS

Right: Back straight, torso level, braced.

Wrong: Lower back rounded over the bar.

Keep your back straight and your torso roughly level with the floor.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Lower back roundsThe lower back rounds over the bar.
  2. Hips tuck underThe hips tuck under as the back curls.
Pull1 s
Lower2 s
Look closer

Grip

Overhand, one hand above the other. Thumbs wrapped around the bar, not alongside it.

Keep the wrists from curling forward.

Common handling mistakes

  • Rounding the lower back

    Fix: Brace before each rep and use a lighter load.

  • Jerking it up

    Fix: Pull with control. Squeeze the shoulder blades at the top.

  • Stopping short at the bottom

    Fix: Lower until the arms are straight.

Where you should feel it

You should feel this between and around your shoulder blades.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • FixBrace first and use a lighter load.

  • FixStop the set. Don't train through the pain.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Anchor a barbell end in a landmine. Load the free end.

  2. 2

    Straddle the loaded end, feet between hip and shoulder width.

  3. 3

    Hinge until the torso is roughly level with the floor, back straight.

  4. 4

    Both hands overhand below the plates, one above the other.

  5. 5

    Beat target by one or two reps? Add 2 to 10 percent.

Risks and when to stop

  • A rounded back strains the lower back and raises the chance of injury.
  • Of the rows tested, the bent-over row loaded the lower spine most.
  • Heavy reps with a held breath send blood pressure very high.

How to do itT-Bar Row

Back line

Right
BACK STRAIGHT
Wrong
BACK ROUNDS

Right: Back straight, chest level with the floor, soft knees.

Wrong: Back rounded over the bar.

Keep your back straight and your chest level with the floor.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Back roundsThe back rounds forward over the bar.
  2. Hips tuck underThe hips tuck under as the back curls.
Pull1 s
Hold1 s
Lower2 s
Look closer

Grip

Palms facing, thumbs wrapped around the V-handle, not alongside it. Straps are fine on heavy sets.

Keep the wrists from curling forward.

Common handling mistakes

  • Rounding the back

    Fix: Brace and use a lighter load.

  • Swinging the weight up

    Fix: Pull the shoulder blades back. Hold the squeeze at the top.

  • Stopping halfway down

    Fix: Lower all the way, slowly, each rep.

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in the middle and sides of your back. Your lower back works hard too.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • FixStop the set. Don't train through the pain.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Barbell in a landmine, plates on the free end.

  2. 2

    Hook a V-handle under the bar about 8-10 inches from the plates.

  3. 3

    Stand over the bar, feet about shoulder width, knees slightly bent.

  4. 4

    Hinge, chest level with the floor. Grab the handle, palms facing.

  5. 5

    Beat target by one or two reps? Add 2 to 10 percent.

Risks and when to stop

  • A rounded back strains the lower back and raises the chance of injury.
  • Without a chest pad the lower back works much harder.
  • Heavy reps with a held breath send blood pressure very high.

Back pain

How to do itBarbell Shrug

Top position

Right
ARMS STRAIGHT
Wrong
ELBOWS BENT

Right: Shoulders up toward the ears, arms straight.

Wrong: Elbows bent, pulling the bar up with the arms.

Keep your elbows straight and let your arms just hang.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Elbows bendThe elbows bend to pull the bar up.
  2. Arms pullThe arms lift the bar instead of the shoulders.
Lift1 s
Lower2 s
Look closer

Grip

Overhand, hands about shoulder width, thumbs wrapped around the bar.

Common handling mistakes

  • Rolling the shoulders

    Fix: Lift straight up, lower straight down.

  • Bending the arms to pull

    Fix: Keep your elbows straight. If you can't, lower the weight.

  • Dropping the bar fast

    Fix: Lower slowly to the start.

Where you should feel it

You should feel this on top of your shoulders, between neck and shoulder.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • FixStop the set.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Overhand grip, hands about shoulder width, thumbs around the bar.

  2. 2

    Stand tall with knees slightly bent and hips straight.

  3. 3

    Let the bar hang in front of your thighs on straight arms.

  4. 4

    Lift your shoulders straight up toward your ears. No rolling.

  5. 5

    Beat target by one or two reps? Add 2 to 10 percent.

Risks and when to stop

  • Heavy reps with a held breath send blood pressure very high.
  • The shoulder is a common injury site in lifting. Poor technique adds risk.

Shoulder pain

Sudden or severe, after falling, or arm won't move? Get it checked today.

Getting worse, very hard to move, or no better after two weeks? See a doctor.

General guidance, not medical advice. If something hurts, stop and get it checked.

How to do itCable Shrug

Top position

Right
ARMS STRAIGHT
Wrong
ELBOWS BENT

Right: Shoulders up, arms straight, standing straight.

Wrong: Elbows bent, curling the bar up.

Keep your arms straight and let only the shoulders lift the bar.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Elbows bendThe elbows bend to curl the bar up.
  2. Arms pullThe arms lift the bar instead of the shoulders.
Lift1 s
Hold1 s
Lower2 s
Look closer

Grip

Overhand, thumbs wrapped around the bar. Wrist bent back in its natural grip position, not curled forward.

Common handling mistakes

  • Curling the bar up

    Fix: Keep the arms straight. Only the shoulders move.

  • Rolling the shoulders

    Fix: Lift straight up, lower straight down.

  • Not standing up straight

    Fix: Stand up straight, head up, eyes forward.

Where you should feel it

You should feel this on top of your shoulders, beside the neck.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • FixKeep the arms straight.

  • FixStop the set. Don't train through the pain.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Bar attachment on the low pulley.

  2. 2

    Overhand grip, hands shoulder width or a little wider.

  3. 3

    Stand close to the pulley, arms straight, bar in front of you.

  4. 4

    Stand up straight, head up, eyes forward.

  5. 5

    Beat target by one or two reps? Add 2 to 10 percent.

Risks and when to stop

  • Heavy reps with a held breath send blood pressure very high.
  • The shoulder is a common injury site in weight training. Poor technique adds risk.

How to do itSmith Machine Shrug

Top position

Right
ARMS LONG
Wrong
ELBOWS BENT

Right: Shoulders up toward the ears, arms long, head level.

Wrong: Elbows bent, pulling the bar up with the arms.

Let your arms hang long with only a slight bend at the elbows.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Head forwardThe head pushes forward as the shoulders rise.
  2. Chin dropsThe chin drops instead of the head staying level.
Lift2 s
Lower2 s
Look closer

Grip

Overhand, hands slightly wider than your shoulders, thumbs wrapped around the bar.

Common handling mistakes

  • Pushing the head forward

    Fix: Keep the head level as the shoulders rise.

  • Rocking the body

    Fix: Use slow, steady reps. Add weight in small steps.

  • Bending the elbows

    Fix: Keep the arms long. Lift with the shoulders.

Where you should feel it

You should feel this between your neck and shoulders.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • FixStop the set. Don't train through the pain.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Set the bar at mid-thigh height.

  2. 2

    Set the safety pins so the bar cannot drop.

  3. 3

    Stand with feet shoulder-width apart.

  4. 4

    Grip overhand, slightly wider than the shoulders, thumbs wrapped.

  5. 5

    Rotate the bar off the hooks and let the arms hang long.

Risks and when to stop

  • Heavy reps with a held breath send blood pressure very high.
  • The shoulder is a common injury site in lifting. Poor technique adds risk.

Shoulder pain

Sudden or severe, after falling, or arm won't move? Get it checked today.
